newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two killed in strike clashes in Pakistani Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in strike clashes in Pakistani Kashmir.

text.p: At least two people were killed and several wounded in gun battles in Pakistan-ruled Kashmir during a transport strike called by the opposition on Thursday, police and witnesses said.
A member of the opposition All-Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference (AJKMC) was killed at Bagh town of Azad (free) Kashmir and a woman was killed by stray bullets near Mirpur town, police said.
Police sources said the death at Bagh occurred during a clash between workers of the AJKMC and former Pakistan prime minister Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) which rules the state.
But PPP Education Minister Qamar Zaman denied the police account and said it was a clash between police and AJKMC workers who were forcing public transport to stay off the roads.
A woman standing on the roof of her house, injured when police fired shots in the air to scare away opposition demonstrators at Pothi, near Mirpur, later died in hospital, residents said.
The AJKMC had called the strike to protest against alleged misrule, a charge denied by state Prime Minister Sultan Mahmood.
AJKMC leader Sardar Abdul Qayyum said he had been placed under house arrest at a state guest house in Muzaffarabad, the state capital.
But Mahmood denied this, and said Qayyum had called for the strike to divert attention from a recent split in his party, with former Azad Kashmir president Sikandar Hayat forming a breakaway faction.
He said the strike had failed.

Azad Kashmir is part of one-third of Kashmir that is controlled by Pakistan. India rules the remaining two-thirds of the region, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
